copy.approvedClaim: Your personal mailbox is stored with zero-access encryption. Liaison's servers and your organisation's admins cannot decrypt it. Mail arriving from the public internet is encrypted the moment it reaches us. It is not end to end encrypted between you and the sender, because standard email is not. Encryption protects the contents from being read. It does not prove who put a message in your mailbox, and it does not hide who you correspond with or when.

copy.agentResidual: When you ask the assistant to read your mail, it reads it in your browser while the mailbox is unlocked. Its answer is stored in the conversation you can see, so what it wrote about your mail stays in that chat history. Liaison counts every message the assistant reads in a session and caps it, and you can turn the assistant's access to this mailbox off entirely below.
copy.rotationNote: Adding a new key does not re-encrypt mail you already have and does not undo an earlier exposure. Old mail keeps opening with the old key, which is what makes it readable at all. Treat a new key as a fresh start, not as a repair.
copy.passphraseCaveat: Liaison stores what opens your mailbox, locked with your mailbox password. Anyone who ever holds that copy can try passwords offline, with no limit on attempts, so make it long and use it nowhere else.
copy.passwordExplainer: Your mailbox password opens your mail on any device. It is not your Liaison login password, and Liaison never sees it.
copy.passkeyShortcut: A passkey lets this device open your mail without typing the mailbox password. Other devices still use the password.

copy.operatorLimit: One limit worth knowing: Liaison serves the JavaScript that does the encrypting. This design stops the servers from reading stored mail. It cannot stop an operator who chooses to serve a different page from collecting keys as you type them.

agentSafety.title: Agent safety
agentSafety.desc: How the agent behaves after it has read text from outside the organization, such as an inbound email, a web page or a result from a connected tool. That text can carry instructions written by a stranger.
agentSafety.untrustedLabel: Ask for approval after outside content
agentSafety.untrustedHelp: On (recommended): once a conversation has read outside content, the agent's actions that leave the organization (sending, replying, posting, paying) and its writes to memory and Knowledge wait for a person to approve them, unless an auto-approve policy covers them.
agentSafety.offNote: Off: the agent acts on outside content without asking. Anyone who can email you or publish a page the agent reads may be able to steer what it sends or saves. Switch it off only if you accept that risk.

aiModels.reasoningDefaultOption: Built-in default (Auto: High, other models: their own default)
